newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises to 10.1 percent.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises to 10.1 percent.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose to 10.1 percent on Wednesday from 9.0 on Tuesday, pushed up by stronger demand in lively trade totalling 23.2 million kuna.
Dealers put demand for fresh kuna funds at 18.7 million kuna, while most deals were made at a 9 percent call money rate.
One 16-30 day interbank loan was made at 13 percent, and another one-month loan was rolled over at 17 percent.
There was no overnight trade given a 326 million kuna surplus left on the banks' accounts.
The central bank's kuna midrates for Thursday eased to 5.5261 to the dollar and firmed slightly to 3.5261 to the German mark. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
